comparator.name: Psychology
comparator.route: Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation (year 3, 24 EC)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations apply to the Dutch and English tracks of the 2024 curriculum. Overview 2 shows three 60 EC study units. The component credits shown here are workload equivalents at 28 hours per credit. Each year is assessed as a study unit through its portfolio and competency exam. The first year combines 32 EC equivalent of psychology cores, 16 of scientific inquiry and 12 of professional skills. The second year combines 16 of Psychological Citizenship, four blocks of 8 each, including the Research Project, and 12 of professional skills. The third year combines 24 of electives, 24 of specialisation and 12 of professional skills. The programme page mentions a thesis, but the regulations give no separate credit allocation or module placement. The Year 2 supervised group Research Project is the identified research component. The 2025–2026 catalogue supports topic-level comparisons for the first two years of this curriculum.

routeSelection.route: Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation (year 3, 24 EC)
routeSelection.basis: The Dutch and English registrations share the 2024 curriculum. The three Year 3 specialisations have equal workload. Brain, Cognition and Behaviour is first in the regulations and the programme overview. The general route leaves elective choices open.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Foundations of psychology: the study of how people think, feel and behave from biological, individual and social perspectives and across the lifespan, taught in the core modules Psychological Perspectives, Individuals in Context and Lifespan Psychology

Brain, cognition and behaviour: functional neuroanatomy and the neuroscience of perception, attention, learning, memory, language, action and motivation, taught in the core module Brain and Cognition and the Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation
Biological and pharmacological bases of behaviour: biopsychology, psychopharmacology and neuropsychology within the Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation
The mind: philosophical and computational perspectives on cognition, taught in the core module Mind (computational thinking, models of the mind, foundational debates of cognitive science)

Research methods, statistics and critical thinking: the Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking modules on biases and fallacies, descriptive and inferential statistics, analysis of variance, regression, reliability and factor analysis, together with research methods and experiments

Programming and computational skills for psychological research, taught in the Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking IV module (procedural programming in Python, algorithms, basic neural networks) and in statistical scripting

Clinical psychology and psychodiagnostics: clinical conditions and their treatment within Lifespan Psychology, psychodiagnostics and psychometrics in year 2, and the Clinical Psychology specialisation
adjacent: Transdisciplinary psychology: applying psychological research to complex societal problems together with neighbouring disciplines, one of the three formal year-3 specialisations
Work and organisational psychology and psychology and economics, named as fields of the transdisciplinary specialisation
Psychology with law and politics (legal psychology, psychology and politics), named as fields of the transdisciplinary specialisation
Health psychology, named as a field of the transdisciplinary specialisation and a stable study direction of the programme
Psychology, engineering and data science, named as neighbouring disciplines of the transdisciplinary specialisation
questions: How can psychology explain, predict and change how people think, feel and behave in order to improve their lives and their mental health?
How can psychological insight help society face climate change and sustainability, migration and inclusion, digital technology, loneliness, polarisation and social justice?

trace: teaches microeconomics (supply and demand, game theory, consumer behaviour) and macroeconomics; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the economic theory that psychology and economics sets against actual behaviour

analyses consumer behaviour, decision making under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations before turning to markets; it makes a specific complementary contribution to psychology and economics

teaches ordinary and generalised least squares and instrumental variables with Monte Carlo simulation and an empirical paper; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the causal-inference and prediction methods of empirical behavioural economics
integrates psychological insight into economic theory, with biases, heuristics and framing studied through experiments; it directly implements psychology and economics

unpacks what drives consumers' behaviour and engagement with brands, including consumer psychology and responsible trust building; it makes a specific complementary contribution as applied consumer psychology

teaches research design, operationalization, experimental design and sampling together with descriptive and inferential statistics and analysis of variance; it directly implements the first Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking modules on research methods and statistics
Examines emotion regulation, emotional labour, belonging and psychological safety in organisations. It provides a workplace perspective on inclusion and wellbeing.

examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations (motivation, personality, perception, decision making, group behaviour, leadership and organisational culture); it directly implements work and organisational psychology
teaches negotiation and persuasion through simulations and role-plays; it makes a specific complementary contribution as applied interpersonal decision making and conflict management in organisations

examines AI ethics and the psychology of AI, including over-trust in and resistance to AI in decision making, empathy and attachment to AI companions and algorithmic bias; it directly implements the question of how digital technology changes human behaviour

teaches planning and decision making under uncertainty and partial observability; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the formal decision-making methods of the engineering and data-science neighbour of psychology

teaches data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation with hands-on work on social-science data sets and ends with an own research project; it directly implements the data-handling and analysis skills that the scientific-inquiry modules develop in scripts

teaches regression, classification, resampling and clustering for understanding data and predicting outcomes; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the data-analysis and prediction methods that the course catalogue says rest on programming in modern behavioural neuroscience

teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python with testing and debugging; it directly implements the procedural programming and algorithmic thinking that Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking IV teaches in Python

examines the drivers of anthropogenic climate change, its impacts on natural systems and the societal transformations it drives; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the climate challenge that the programme names as a problem psychologists help address

teaches how cognitive biases and social pressures make people vulnerable to misinformation and how to evaluate claims and scientific credibility; it directly implements the critical-thinking strand of Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking I, which addresses biases, fallacies and illusions

offers legal, social and normative perspectives on law, from constitutional and criminal law to human rights; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the social-justice question and to the law that the transdisciplinary specialisation connects with psychology
studies human rights as positive law, history and philosophy; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the social-justice and inclusion challenges the programme names

teaches criminal accountability, guilt, justification and excuse and the presumption of innocence; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the criminal-law framework with which legal psychology works

asks what consciousness is, whether the mind can be explained neurobiologically and whether artificial systems can be conscious; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the foundational debates about the mind that the Mind core module addresses

gives the analytical tools to compare political systems and explain growing dissatisfaction and support for parties at the political extremes; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the political dimension of polarisation and of psychology and politics
examines theories of conflict and peacebuilding drawing on sociology, political science and law; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the study of social division and polarisation

teaches sociological concepts, methods and theories for analysing everyday interaction, institutions and social structure; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the social-structural perspective that the transdisciplinary specialisation combines with psychology

teaches the design, data collection, analysis and interpretation of qualitative research on how people make sense of social processes; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the method for studying societal problems that quantitative methods do not capture

studies social-movement theories and environmental justice with feminist, anti-colonial and degrowth perspectives and civic engagement; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the social-justice and climate questions
examines civil society, solidarity, social capital and social trust; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the questions of social connection and social division

teaches the principles of pharmacology, drug targets, pharmacokinetics and the neuronal, hormonal and cellular regulation that drugs affect; it makes a specific complementary contribution to psychopharmacology as a general pharmacology course rather than a course on psychoactive drugs

relates normal function and pathophysiology for six organ systems including the central nervous system; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the neurological side of neuropsychology, without covering psychiatric disorders

studies the evolution of brains, brain regions and rhythms that regulate behaviour, animal models, research ethics and disorders, with laboratory work; it directly implements the biological and neuroscientific side of Brain and Cognition

examines the neural mechanisms of perception and action and uses methods of cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology; it directly implements the perception and action themes of the Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation

treats memory, attention, emotion, social cognition, consciousness and decision making in depth with neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and experimental approaches; it directly implements learning, memory and attention in the Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation

studies the neuroscience and psychology of language comprehension, production, impairment and acquisition with hands-on experiments; it directly implements the language processing that Brain and Cognition lists among the cognitive functions

teaches cell biology, molecular biology, cellular physiology and communication and genetics and evolution, with a research-presentation assignment; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the cellular and genetic foundation of the biology of behaviour, and it is the formal prerequisite for the pharmacology, physiology and disease-mechanisms courses of this programme

introduces the psychological and neuroscientific study of why people behave as they do, with brain areas, neuronal communication, brain injury and the interplay of nature and nurture; it directly implements the broad introduction to psychology from biological, individual and social perspectives

teaches the normal function of organ systems, including the nervous and endocrine systems, homeostasis and cell signalling; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the physiological basis of biopsychology

covers the main theories and findings of social psychology (social cognition, attitudes, groups, interpersonal behaviour and social influence); it directly implements the social-psychological strand of Individuals in Context

teaches multivariate models (linear regression, ANOVA and ANCOVA, factor analysis, logistic regression) and non-parametric tests with experimental methods; it directly implements the statistical analysis of experimental designs and the factor analysis of the Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking modules

covers mental disorders across the lifespan from a bio-psycho-social perspective, including prevalence, assessment, diagnosis, classification and treatment; it directly implements the clinical conditions that Lifespan Psychology addresses

examines the bio-psycho-social interplay in health and illness and psychological interventions in medical settings; it makes a specific complementary contribution as clinical health psychology applied to the programme's clinical conditions
teaches clinical psychological assessment, psychodiagnostics with its ethical issues and the main psychotherapy approaches; it directly implements the psychodiagnostic strand of the programme
teaches systematic reviews and meta-analysis with hands-on analysis in R; it makes a specific complementary contribution as research synthesis and statistical scripting for psychological research
examines physical, cognitive, social and emotional development from pregnancy to older age, including attachment and some assessment and intervention; it directly implements lifespan psychology

has students join an international research project and develop evidence-based materials that strengthen young people's resilience to radicalisation through empathy, civic engagement and mental well-being; it directly implements applied psychological research on polarisation and well-being

analyses how the climate crisis is communicated and contested through texts, media, protest and social media and ends in a project that enters the debate; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the communication of the climate challenge

teaches persuasion, framing, nudging and cognitive shortcuts drawing on social psychology and neuroscience, with the ethics of persuasion and a community project; it makes a specific complementary contribution to how behaviour is influenced in public debate on societal problems

Uses study designs, confounding, association and causal reasoning to investigate disease patterns and appraise population-health evidence. This complements experimental psychology with observational study methods.

alternatives.label: Psychology, Brain and Cognition
alternatives.labelReason: Study how people think, develop and behave. Combine social and developmental psychology with neuroscience, psycholinguistics, mental health and research methods, including experiments, statistics and data analysis.
alternatives.concept: Study how people think, develop and behave. Combine social and developmental psychology with neuroscience, psycholinguistics, mental health and research methods, including experiments, statistics and data analysis.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes cognitive science. Programming and introductory data science precede machine learning, and physiology precedes disease mechanisms. Research Methods & Statistics and Statistics & Experimental Methods precede research synthesis.

alternatives.label: Psychology and Societal Challenges
alternatives.labelReason: Study behaviour in the context of climate change, inclusion, technology and social division. Combine psychology with sociology, communication, law and empirical research on public problems.
alternatives.concept: Study behaviour in the context of climate change, inclusion, technology and social division. Combine psychology with sociology, communication, law and empirical research on public problems.
progression: The brain and behavioural foundation precedes specialist mental health and research. Empirical methods precede research synthesis. Sociology precedes advanced social theory.
alternatives.distinctness: This plan develops behaviour in the context of climate, persuasion, polarisation, social justice and youth resilience. It adds sociology, rights, environmental justice and climate communication in place of much of the closest option’s biological and cognitive science.
traceOverrides: introduces the psychological and neuroscientific study of why people behave as they do and how behaviour can be predicted and changed; it directly implements the foundation of psychology on which the societal applications are built
teaches research design, sampling and descriptive and inferential statistics; it directly implements the research and statistics foundation for evaluating evidence on societal problems
covers social cognition, attitudes, groups and social influence; it directly implements the social psychology needed to understand polarisation, social division and social connection

covers the prevalence and development of mental disorders and the cultural, gender and environmental factors that shape mental health; it directly implements the mental-health challenge that the programme names

examines human development across the lifespan, including social and emotional development and ageing; it directly implements lifespan psychology and makes a specific complementary contribution to questions of loneliness and social connection across life stages
teaches multivariate statistical models and experimental methods; it directly implements the quantitative analysis of complex behavioural data

examines biological, psychological and socio-cultural influences on health and illness and interventions in medical settings; it directly implements health psychology as one of the societal applications of psychology

teaches systematic reviews and meta-analysis and explains their use in evidence-based policy making; it directly implements the step from psychological research findings to evidence that can inform societal decisions

teaches how cognitive biases and social pressures make people vulnerable to misinformation, fake news and pseudoscience; it directly implements the psychology of misinformation in digital and political debate

alternatives.label: Applied Psychology, Organisations and Decision-Making
alternatives.labelReason: Study decisions and behaviour in organisations and markets. Combine psychology with economics, law, negotiation and data analysis, and use research methods to evaluate evidence about behaviour.
alternatives.concept: Study decisions and behaviour in organisations and markets. Combine psychology with economics, law, negotiation and data analysis, and use research methods to evaluate evidence about behaviour.
progression: Economics precedes microeconomics and behavioural economics. Law precedes criminal law, and programming precedes AI decision-making. Social psychology precedes organisational psychology.
alternatives.distinctness: This plan studies decisions through behavioural economics, econometrics, organisational psychology, negotiation and criminal law. Its methods and applications differ from the cognitive and biomedical depth of the closest plan and the public and civic focus of the societal option.
traceOverrides: teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python; it directly implements the programming skill that connects psychology with engineering and data science

offers legal, social and normative perspectives on law, including criminal law and human rights; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the gateway to the law with which legal psychology works
teaches research design, sampling and descriptive and inferential statistics; it directly implements the research and statistics foundation for the applied fields
introduces the psychological and neuroscientific study of why people behave as they do; it directly implements the foundation of psychology that the applied fields build on
covers social cognition, attitudes, groups and interpersonal behaviour; it directly implements the social psychology underlying group behaviour in organisations and markets

examines AI ethics and the psychology of AI, including over-trust in AI in decision making and algorithmic bias; it directly implements the human-centred questions that connect psychology with engineering and data science
teaches multivariate statistical models and experimental methods; it directly implements the quantitative analysis used in applied psychological and behavioural-economic research

examines biological, psychological and socio-cultural influences on health and illness and interventions in medical settings; it directly implements health psychology, named as a field of the transdisciplinary specialisation
teaches systematic reviews and meta-analysis and explains their use in evidence-based policy making; it directly implements the evidence synthesis that applied psychological research relies on
teaches data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation and ends with an own research project; it directly implements the data-science side of psychology, engineering and data science

treats memory, attention, emotion, social cognition and decision making in depth; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the cognitive basis of judgement and decision making studied in psychology and economics
teaches regression, classification, resampling and clustering for prediction; it directly implements the machine-learning side of psychology, engineering and data science
gives the analytical tools to compare political systems and explain political behaviour and dissatisfaction; it makes a specific complementary contribution to psychology and politics
Examines emotion regulation, emotional labour, belonging and psychological safety at work.

candidates.label: Clinical psychology and mental health care
Applied and transdisciplinary psychology: work, economics, law, politics and data science

selection.assessment: Three plans sustain different progressions in brain and cognition, behaviour and societal challenges, and psychology of organisations and decisions. All pairwise differences exceed 30 EC. A clinical direction was tested separately. Psychopathology, psychodiagnostics, therapy approaches, health psychology and pharmacology contribute real clinical subject matter. They are concentrated in the closest option. Adding general ethics, qualitative methods and epidemiology would add context, with insufficient dedicated training in psychological test construction, therapeutic interviewing, care assessment or supervised intervention to sustain a separate option.

blocks: Foundations of psychology: perspectives, social and developmental psychology
Both introduce biological and social perspectives on behaviour. UCR emphasises brain and behaviour. Maastricht brings in a wider range of psychological perspectives.
Both study social cognition and group behaviour. Maastricht also examines personality and individual differences.
Both study cognitive, emotional and social development across the lifespan.
Brain, cognition and the biology of behaviour
Both connect the brain to behaviour. UCR uses comparative neurobiology and laboratory methods. Maastricht also studies imaging and brain stimulation.
Both study memory and attention with experimental approaches. Maastricht also examines perception as prediction.
Both study how the brain guides action. UCR focuses on perception and motor control. Maastricht also studies motivation.
Maastricht offers a dedicated cognitive neuroscience methods module. UCR uses related methods within perception and cognition courses.
Both examine how drugs act. UCR covers pharmacology across body systems. Maastricht focuses on the biology of behaviour and psychoactive drugs.
Both examine questions about the mind. UCR focuses on philosophy of mind. Maastricht also studies computational models of cognition.
Both study psychological assessment and its ethical implications. UCR adds psychotherapy approaches. Maastricht also develops psychometric analysis.
Research methods, statistics, programming and critical thinking
Both examine biases, fallacies and the evaluation of claims. UCR focuses on misinformation and scientific credibility.
Both introduce research methods and statistics. UCR includes research design, surveys and analysis of variance.
Both study statistical models for experimental data. UCR uses regression, variance analysis and related methods.
Both develop programming in Python. UCR also covers object-oriented programming. Maastricht applies programming to examples from psychology.
Maastricht uses a supervised small-group project covering the empirical research cycle. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the scheduled courses.
Both apply psychological research to societal problems. UCR focuses on youth radicalisation and resilience. Maastricht covers a broader range of problems and perspectives.
Economics, organisations, law, politics and decision-making with data
Professional skills, portfolio and open elective space
UCR develops academic writing, research literacy and civic engagement. Maastricht includes a programme of psychology-specific professional skills and portfolio work.
Maastricht develops psychology-specific professional communication and reflective practice.
Maastricht includes a third year of professional and life skills alongside a competency portfolio.
Maastricht students choose 24 EC of electives. Options include faculty courses or an approved external package.

notes.text: Maastricht includes dedicated cognitive neuroscience methods, psychology-specific professional skills, a supervised empirical project and a 24 EC specialisation. UCR covers related subjects across psychology, brain and behaviour, statistics and neighbouring disciplines.

Maastricht assesses each 60 EC year as a study unit through a portfolio and competency exam. The programme overview mentions a Year 3 thesis, and the regulations list no separate thesis credit allocation. UCR’s optional independent research is separate from the scheduled coursework.

audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht’s Psychology bachelor combines the study of behaviour and the brain with research methods and professional skills.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The 2026–2027 example follows the Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation. Maastricht awards credits by study year. The table breaks each year down by the published workload. UCR offers three related ways to study psychology.
